task.description: REWORK REQUIRED. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR read deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex.ex lines 400-583 (v0.15.1, confirmed in mix.lock) directly and found: the design's SS5.2 claim that do_fail/5's exit({:script_failed, ...}) 'crashes the Wasmex instance process directly' is FALSE. wasmex's handle_info/2 (line 542) wraps the apply(callback, [context | params]) call (line 557) in a try/rescue/catch block; a bare `catch kind, reason ->` clause with an UNBOUND kind catches exit/1 exactly like :throw or :error (standard, documented Elixir behavior -- Kernel.SpecialForms.try/1's own docs use exactly this example). So exit({:script_failed, ...}) is caught right there: success=false, results=[Exception.format_banner(:exit, {:script_failed, ...})], instance_receive_callback_result/3 is called with success=false via the ORDINARY callback-failure path, and handle_info/2 returns {:noreply, state} -- the Wasmex instance process does NOT crash and does NOT terminate. This invalidates: SS5.2 (the mechanism claim itself), SS5.3 (the expected GenServer.call crash-shape -- there is no crash to propagate; Wasmex.call_function/4 most likely returns an ordinary {:error, _} indistinguishable in KIND from a guest trap, since both surface via the same NIF failure path), SS8.2 (WASM-side normalization of fail via an {:exit,...} observation that doesn't exist), SS9.5 (wrong characterization of the Lua/WASM difference -- the real difference is that Lua's fail crashes its process while WASM's fail, AS CURRENTLY DESIGNED, does not crash at all and looks like an ordinary guest trap), and SS2's third discard-mechanism bullet (same false crash claim). Most seriously: this threatens AC5 itself -- if fail is caught by the same generic catch clause an ordinary runtime error inside a callback hits, fail and a guest trap may be STRUCTURALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE at the Wasmex.call_function/4 boundary, exactly the ambiguity AC5 requires you to rule out, not accidentally reproduce. You must find and design a mechanism that actually makes fail uninterceptable and distinguishable from an ordinary trap -- live-verify whatever mechanism you choose against the real wasmex source and/or a real minimal repro (e.g. a small Elixir script calling Wasmex.call_function/4 with a callback that does exit(...) vs one that raises, and inspecting the actual returned/observed shapes) before writing it into the design as fact. Options worth investigating (verify, don't assume): tagging the failure result/reason itself so it's inspectable and distinguishable downstream even though it arrives via the same {:error,...} path as a trap; having do_fail/5 send an out-of-band signal (e.g. to the calling task) before or instead of exit/1; or another mechanism you identify from reading the actual dependency. Re-verify SS2's discard-mechanism table for internal consistency once fail's real mechanism is known -- PluginHandler.run_guest/3's unconditional GenServer.stop/1 on any path where call_export/3 returns was flagged by the validator as possibly now applying to fail's path too, since fail may no longer crash the process; check this doesn't create a NEW indistinguishability between fail and a guest trap now that both discard via the same stop/1 call. The validator explicitly did not complete its remaining 6 checks (other failure-arm discard mechanisms, call_service distinguishability, exhaustiveness guard, remaining SS9 entries, Lua-file-untouched confirmation) since one confirmed defect was sufficient for FAIL -- treat this as a fresh full pass, not a patch of only SS5/SS8.2/SS9.5/SS2.
acceptance_criteria: ONE shared scenario definition is executed against BOTH the Lua executor and the WASM handler, asserting identical observable outcomes -- WASM-12's own acceptance criterion -- rather than two separately written suites; the shared harness is a single named module or fixture, quoted in the moduledoc

a test asserts a guest that writes variables and then FAILS leaves instance variable state unchanged, asserted separately for each failure arm: a guest trap, fuel exhaustion (REQ-169), memory cap (REQ-169), wall-clock timeout (REQ-170), and fail
a test asserts a guest that writes several variables and succeeds applies all of them with no observable partial state

a test asserts call_service returns a structured error to the guest on service failure rather than trapping, and a separate test asserts a missing service capability fails per REQ-167 -- the two behaviours asserted distinctly
a test asserts a guest that attempts to catch or ignore its own fail STILL yields a failed outcome and does not run to completion -- the WASM analogue of REQ-161's uninterceptable-termination test

any semantic difference between the Lua and WASM host APIs that is not purely ABI (string encoding, return shape) is enumerated explicitly in the moduledoc with its justification; the moduledoc states that WASM-12 limits differences to ABI, so an unlisted one means the requirement is unmet

the moduledoc states that the Lua host API is the definition WASM conforms to per decision 0014 Decision (4), and that no Lua-side behaviour was changed to ease parity; confirmed by `git diff --stat` scoped to this requirement's commits showing no Lua host-API implementation file modified
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
